Mercafacil: transforming campaign creation

+Retail marketing platform serving millions of customers. Research showed manual work, not lack of guidance, was blocking campaign launches.

Problem

Customers struggled to create and launch marketing campaigns. The early assumption was that they needed more guidance.

Insight

Usage data, support tickets and interviews pointed elsewhere: excessive manual work was the real barrier.

What I did

  • Analyzed product usage data and support tickets
  • Interviewed customers and mapped existing journeys
  • Facilitated ideation with stakeholders
  • Designed and tested prototypes
  • Built a Redash dashboard combining Google Analytics and campaign database data

Worked with

Product and Engineering on definition and delivery. Project: Campanha da Maria (offers pipeline). Role: Senior Product Designer (Jun 2020 – Oct 2023, remote). I also built the company’s design system.

Outcome

  • Reached 4 million users with an in-house AI project that lifted campaign sales revenue by 180%
  • Became one of the platform’s three most-used features
  • Became a significant revenue source
  • One solution helped recover a previously lost customer
  • Improvements to the product experience grew the user base by 230%
  • Identified a USD 30,600 revenue gap and produced an at-risk customer list with next steps to close it

Lessons

Smaller deliveries would have brought value earlier. Including Support and CS made a big difference in understanding what users needed. People without the users’ context get little from workshops: even when given the context, they need the customers’ lived experience to understand it.

Rentcars: improving conversion through experience design

+The results page (“Listar”) put a wall of checkboxes between travelers and a car. Research on filters, categories, recommendations and sorting led to a redesign that contributed to a 3% conversion increase.

Problem

Customers are usually in a hurry. Critical filters such as automatic transmission were buried or missing, and the page was crowded with options. If users can’t find what they need quickly, they leave.

Goals

  • Update and prioritize essential filters
  • Make sorting clearer and customer-centric
  • Simplify multistore results
  • Check the clarity of the recommended section

Research

  • Clarity (18 May – 18 Jun 2025) and BigQuery (3 – 23 Jun 2025) analysis of real usage
  • 5 moderated tests with people who had rented before: Argentina, Mexico, Germany, USA, Brazil
  • 5 unmoderated Maze tests with Brazilian users
  • Support calls from customers who gave up after reading reviews elsewhere

What the data showed

  • Category, especially Economy, is the most-clicked filter; passenger capacity and unlimited mileage come next
  • “Lowest price first” is the most-used sort
  • Map and protection add-ons got little interaction at the search stage
  • Many participants said they wouldn’t use filters and would search more specifically instead

Decisions

  • Benchmarked competitors’ categories, found different names for the same cars, calculated average daily prices per overlapping category and merged those with similar fleets and prices
  • Replaced car-specific images with generic illustrations, so a category isn’t mistaken for an offer, and added a leaf symbol to Economy
  • Filters: most used first, characteristics split into their own category, single-option filters hidden, all filters multi-select
  • Sorting: renamed “Recommended” and “Best store rating” to clearer labels
  • Recommendations kept above filters, with micro-copy explaining why

What users told us

“I don’t really know what the difference between economic and compact is.” (participant, 43)

“Sorting by ‘Recommended’ feels like a black box. Is it sponsored? Algorithmic?” (participant, 49)

Terminology

“Shuttle” was not understood, Spanish speakers expect “Transmisión” rather than “cambio”, and “petrol” and “gas” vary by dialect.

Outcome

I led the redesign of a core interface, combining user research and data analysis, and it resulted in a 3% increase in sales conversion. Next idea from the research: bring real traveler comments into the rental evaluation. We ran an A/B test by market corridor for a few weeks, then rolled it out to the whole user base.

Rentcars Affiliates: AI-assisted prototyping

+An affiliates dashboard prototyped end to end in Figma Make and validated with users.

What I did

Used Figma Make to prototype the full flow, explore solutions and validate it with users. This was AI-assisted prototyping, not production software development.

Why it matters

Shorter iteration cycles and a working artifact the team could react to, instead of static descriptions. Using Ant Design cut development from months to weeks, and the ease of use won back the trust of our customers and users.

Rentcars Marketplace: field research and design proposals

+Interviews with store administrators in five countries, turned into design proposals and a prioritized roadmap.

Problem

Customer experience challenges and operational inefficiencies in the Marketplace. The research focused on fleet availability, access to store information and the work of configuring promotions, prices and discounts.

Method

Five qualitative interviews with store administrators (Argentina, Chile, Italy, Sri Lanka, Brazil), plus usage data such as heatmaps and click areas.

What we heard

  • Dashboard KPIs matter little: they track numbers in their own systems, and want ticket status and SLA on the dashboard
  • Promotions take too long to activate, so they change the base rate themselves
  • They want self-service control of fleet groups; obsolete groups trigger false low-availability alerts
  • Availability and pricing belong on one screen; multi-store partners rely on spreadsheets
  • Multi-store admins can’t close all stores at once, and prices must include taxes in markets like Chile

Insights

  • Clarity: unclear what updates instantly and where to get support
  • Delays: some features are ignored because of synchronization lag
  • Manual labor: partners spend most of the week updating availability and prices

Design proposals

  • Dashboard notifications and a leaner set of metrics
  • Transparency about what updates instantly
  • Company-level data instead of store-by-store entry
  • Real-time editing of rates and availability in the interface
  • One-way route configuration with exception rules and custom fees

Priorities

Nine next steps, from easier access between stores and a unified rates-and-availability update to instant promotion entry, ticket SLA visibility, fleet autonomy and showing the deposit on the voucher. Impact: higher productivity for rental companies and less internal support time spent with them, as they became more autonomous.

Lexter: building a better SaaS product experience

+A live SaaS product with a trial experience, where research shaped strategy.

What I did

  • Restructured personas and synthesized research insights
  • Influenced strategic product direction
  • Designed a strategic feature
  • Created a Design Partner Program for continuous customer feedback

Outcome

Sr Product Designer, Sep 2024 – May 2025, remote. The persona restructuring produced insights that influenced a strategic shift in company direction. I led the design of strategic features from problem to final solution. We redefined the ICP and focused on a group with a higher profit margin, and from that we built an AI chat that triages our customers’ clients.

Research: “Lexter user vs. everyone else” (2024)

A qualified sample survey of 207 lawyers (80% confidence, 5% margin), plus desk research, netnography and in-depth interviews mapping the lawyer’s journey, with the data triangulated.

  • Non-lawyers subscribe too, and freelancers work through Lexter
  • Lexter today plays the role of an intern
  • Current users want more clients but have no time to think about how to win them
  • Clients in smaller cities contact lawyers more often to ask about their case

Atendimento: where conversations handled by the AI assistant are managed

Atendimento triages the end clients of Lexter’s customers: each conversation is directed by type of matter, with an AI analysis that saves the lawyer time.

Research and strategy in practice

Two pieces of Mercafacil work that aren’t full case studies but show how I research and frame product problems.

Product gaps business case

A business case I built to understand Mercafacil’s product gaps and where revenue was being left behind. The slide frames R$ 153,045.54 as churn driven by engagement and product, avoidable if someone looked at those reasons. I found it by looking at the company’s metrics and contacting customers who had churned, drawing on deep knowledge of the product and its customers.

Research on new offers

Research in two phases, “Quero vender” and “Jornada para novas ofertas”, into how customers define products and run campaigns. Method: conversations with customers and shadowing, to decide what to run and which numbers customers need in the morning to make decisions. We ran only those with insights and left the rest reactive, cutting processing costs.

Cultural differences framework

A Hofstede-based analysis (Jul 2025) of how indulgence, uncertainty avoidance and power distance shape online purchase behavior. It starts from the hypothesis that adapting the product to each region improves conversion, and ends with do’s and don’ts per country (Brazil, Mexico, UK, US, Colombia, Italy and others). We used it to define communication and interface differences for each market corridor.

Leadership and product thinking

Created structure where there was none

I was the first Product Owner at Mercafacil and introduced Scrum to an organization that hadn’t used it. I facilitated ceremonies and coordinated product work for several years.

Owned the design function

For a period I was the company’s only designer, responsible for the whole practice. I later guided and supported teams of up to five designers.

Aligned senior stakeholders

I work directly with business leadership, using evidence from data, support and interviews to challenge assumptions, as in the Mercafacil campaign work.

Bridged design, product and engineering

Day-to-day collaboration with Product, Engineering and Data, including distributed teams in the UK, India and the United States.

Leadership here is hands-on: strategy and process, plus the detailed design work. At Mercafacil I mentored a colleague through a career change, helped interview and hire new designers, and built the design system. At Rentcars I built a global research framework and a central insights repository.

AI and the future of product design

I use AI to increase leverage, not to replace design judgment. People still decide what’s worth building.

Research synthesis

Faster clustering of interview and ticket data, with the evidence checked by me. Tools I use: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

Rapid prototyping

Functional prototypes in Figma Make, as in Rentcars Affiliates, so teams react to something working.

Design exploration

Wider option sets early, narrowed by user evidence and product constraints.

Workflow automation

Product-side AI too: Mercafacil’s in-house AI project reached 4 million users. For prototypes I also use Lovable and Claude Design. I automated the creation of skeleton loaders, componentization and the breakdown of flows through the Figma MCP.
